subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Ionic bonding is best described as:
options: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
Attraction between nuclei and delocalised electrons
questions.explain: Ionic bonds form between metals and non-metals by electron transfer, producing oppositely charged ions.

questions.q: When sodium reacts with chlorine, the sodium atom:
options: Loses one electron to form Na+
questions.explain: Sodium loses its outer electron to achieve a stable configuration, forming Na+; chlorine gains it to form Cl-.

questions.q: Ionic compounds have high melting points because:
options: Strong electrostatic forces act throughout the giant lattice
Molecules are held by weak forces
questions.explain: Much energy is needed to overcome the many strong attractions in the ionic lattice.

questions.q: Molten sodium chloride conducts electricity because:
options: Ions are free to move and carry charge
questions.explain: When molten or dissolved, ions become mobile; solid ionic compounds do not conduct because ions are fixed.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed by:
options: A shared pair of electrons between atoms
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form between non-metals sharing electron pairs.

questions.q: How many bonding pairs are shared in a nitrogen molecule (N2)?
questions.explain: N2 shares three electron pairs, forming a strong triple bond.

questions.q: Using VSEPR theory, the shape of a methane (CH4) molecule is:
questions.explain: Four bonding pairs around carbon repel to a tetrahedral arrangement.

questions.q: The shape of a water molecule and its bond angle is:
questions.explain: Two lone pairs on oxygen repel more strongly, reducing the H-O-H angle to ~104.5 degrees.

questions.q: A covalent bond is polar when the two bonded atoms have:
questions.explain: Unequal electronegativity produces an unequal sharing of electrons and a bond dipole.

questions.q: The strongest type of intermolecular force is:
questions.explain: Among intermolecular forces, hydrogen bonding (F, O or N with H) is strongest; ionic bonding is not an intermolecular force.

questions.q: Which substance can form hydrogen bonds between its molecules?
questions.explain: Hydrogen bonding requires H bonded to N, O or F; ammonia (N-H) qualifies.

questions.q: Diamond has a very high melting point because it is a:
options: Giant covalent structure with strong bonds throughout
questions.explain: In diamond every carbon is covalently bonded to four others in a giant network, needing huge energy to break.

questions.q: Metallic bonding is described as:
options: Attraction between a lattice of cations and delocalised electrons
questions.explain: A 'sea' of delocalised electrons holds metal cations together.

questions.q: Metals conduct electricity because they contain:
options: Delocalised electrons that are free to move
questions.explain: Delocalised electrons carry charge through the metal lattice.

questions.q: Metals are malleable because:
options: Layers of cations can slide over each other while the electron sea holds them together
questions.explain: The non-directional metallic bonding lets layers shift without shattering.

questions.q: The three bonding types (ionic, covalent, metallic) are best viewed as:
options: A continuum, with many compounds showing intermediate character
questions.explain: A bonding triangle shows a continuum, with polar covalent and partially ionic character in between.

questions.q: An alloy is:
options: A mixture of a metal with other elements
questions.explain: Alloys (e.g. steel, brass) have different-sized atoms that disrupt layers, often making them harder than pure metals.

questions.q: Alloys are often harder than pure metals because:
options: Different-sized atoms disrupt the regular layers, hindering sliding
questions.explain: Irregular packing makes it harder for layers of atoms to slip past each other.

questions.q: Carbon dioxide (CO2) has a low boiling point despite strong covalent bonds because:
options: It is a simple molecular substance with weak forces between molecules
It is a giant covalent structure
questions.explain: Only weak London forces act between CO2 molecules, so little energy separates them.

questions.q: What is the formula of the ionic compound formed between magnesium (Mg2+) and chloride (Cl-)?
questions.explain: Charges balance when one Mg2+ combines with two Cl- ions.
